rationale: Lycopolitan reflex of ⲗⲱϩⲙ̄ 'wet, mire, slime.' In this kephalaion's cosmic-botanical question, ⲗⲓϩⲙⲉ is the medium through which life rises from the earth to the firmaments — the sap-like vehicle of cosmic vivification. The plural ⲛ̄ⲗⲓϩⲙⲉ suggests multiple wet/sap-bearing strata.

Verbal compound ⲣ̄- + ⲭⲁⲓⲥ where ⲭⲁⲓⲥ = Lycopolitan ⲭⲱⲥ/ϫⲟⲉⲓⲥ 'lord' (already in accumulated vocabulary). Construction parallels ⲣ̄-ⲡⲟ 'reign' (also in vocab). The astral powers 'are made lord' over flesh and Five Trees from above — a key term for spatial/hierarchical dominion-from-above without earthly rooting.

Idiomatic possessive without preposition: ⲡⲧⲣⲟⲭⲟⲥ ⲛⲟⲩⲛⲉ = 'the Wheel('s) root' / 'a root of the Wheel.' Used in negative construction ⲙⲛ̄ⲧⲉ ⲡⲧⲣⲟⲭⲟⲥ ⲛⲟⲩⲛⲉ ϩⲙ̄ ⲡⲓⲕⲁϩ = 'the Wheel has no root in this earth.' Manichaean cosmological term: the Wheel of stars/zodiac is bound only at the boundary of the sea (line 24), not rooted in earthly soil.

Lycopolitan orthographic variant of ⲍⲱⲇⲓⲟⲛ / ⲍⲱⲇⲟⲛ (already in accumulated vocabulary as 'zodiac-sign'). The ϩ-onset for ζ and -ⲁⲓⲟⲛ for -ⲓⲟⲛ are dialectal features. Singular ⲡⲧϩⲱⲁⲓⲟⲛ (line 15) refers to 'the zodiac' as collective astrological frame; plural ⲛϩⲱⲁⲓⲟⲛ to the individual signs.

Verb of uncertain root governing both archonic corpses (line 21, 3pl) and Hyle herself (line 27, 3sg.f). Consistent with Manichaean cosmogonic acts of casting-down/spreading-out fallen substance. Possibly Lyc reflex of ⲡⲱⲣϣ 'spread out,' ⲡⲁϩⲣ 'cast forth,' or a related expulsion-verb. Flag for parallels.

Verb in line 29 between Hyle's failure to grasp and her fall: ⲙ̄ⲡⲉⲥⲧⲉϩⲁⲥ ⲁⲥⲛⲁⲩϩⲥ̄ ⲁⲥϩⲉⲓ̈ⲉ. Possibly Lyc reflex of ⲛⲟⲩϩ 'shake, sway' or ⲛⲟⲩϫ 'cast.' Could read 'she shook (herself)' or 'she was hurled.' Confidence low.
